title: Không chỉ là bóng đèn
englishTitle: More Than a Light Bulb
paragraphs: Thomas Edison did not invent the first idea of electric light. Other inventors had worked on it before him. Edison and his team helped develop practical incandescent lighting as part of a wider system. Something more than a glowing bulb was needed. Wires, switches and a supply of electricity had to work together.
Edison không nghĩ ra ánh sáng điện đầu tiên. Ông và nhóm phát triển chiếu sáng thực dụng trong cả hệ thống nguồn điện, dây và công tắc.

Imagine an evening room before and after an electric lamp is installed. The furniture, carpet, cupboard and mirror may be the same, but using the room can feel different. A bright room can feel welcoming. Someone can read when the space outside the house is dark. The outside has not changed, but the light inside has.
Căn phòng giả định có cùng nội thất nhưng cách sử dụng buổi tối thay đổi khi có đèn.

An upstairs bedroom and a downstairs sitting room both need connections if both are to receive power. An outside light also belongs to the system. A button or switch is only the visible control. A broken connection may need someone to fix it. An empty socket will not light the room. These examples explain the idea of a system; they are not instructions for electrical repairs.
Các phòng và đèn ngoài nhà đều cần kết nối. Đây là ví dụ về hệ thống, không hướng dẫn sửa điện.

Electric light gradually became part of ordinary home life. It could support a new daily schedule, an everyday reading habit and a more comfortable evening. Yet no single invention creates an ideal lifestyle for everybody. You can shut the door, keep the windows shut, leave a shop closed, or lock a door with a lock; none of those actions alone supplies electricity. The familiar glow depends on work beyond the room. Remembering the team and the connected equipment gives a fuller story than imagining one person simply holding up a bulb and changing every house at once.
Ánh sáng dần đổi thói quen nhưng không tự tạo đời sống lý tưởng cho tất cả. Cần nhớ cả đội ngũ và hạ tầng, thay vì câu chuyện một người với một bóng đèn.

title: Vì sao quần jeans có những miếng kim loại nhỏ?
englishTitle: Why Jeans Have Tiny Metal Parts
paragraphs: In 1873, Jacob Davis and Levi Strauss received a patent for strengthening pocket openings with metal rivets. Denim pants already existed, but the extra support helped at places under strain. An old blue pair of jeans can tell a design story. The little metal parts were not originally just decorations.
Năm 1873, Davis và Strauss được cấp bằng sáng chế gia cố miệng túi bằng đinh tán. Quần denim đã có; cải tiến ở các điểm chịu lực.

Work clothing faces pulling, bending and heavy use. A pocket can tear where it joins the cloth. A thin piece of material may need help at that point. This is a different problem from choosing a suit, a tie, a belt or a matching sock for a formal occasion. A work uniform has to do a job as well as create an appearance.
Quần áo lao động cần chịu kéo và cử động. Bài toán độ bền khác việc chọn trang phục trang trọng.

For a learning example, imagine a family sorting clothes after a wash. The washing includes jeans, a towel and two shirts. An adult customer checks one pair; a teenage customer checks another. The twin sisters have similar jeans, and each twin wants the right pair. One says, “This pair is mine; is that one yours?” Another pair is hers, while the jacket is his. These speakers are invented, not historical customers.
Gia đình phân loại đồ sau giặt là ví dụ hư cấu để học từ và đại từ sở hữu, không phải khách hàng lịch sử.

They tidy the room, tie a bundle and pack it. Everything looks tidy. One sister with curly hair is interested in how the rivets work, rather than only how the jeans look. She is interested in the design because it solves a practical problem. The family may play a favourite single while they work. Whether someone plans to marry is irrelevant to the strength of a single pocket. Clothes carry social meanings, but this invention began with a very physical question: how can a weak point survive more pulling?
Ví dụ kết nối sinh hoạt với câu hỏi thật về thiết kế: gia cố điểm yếu để chịu lực kéo lâu hơn.

title: Những chiếc răng đóng chiếc túi
englishTitle: The Teeth That Close a Bag
paragraphs: A zipper joins two rows of small elements as a slider moves along them. It is easy to overlook this everyday mechanism. Gideon Sundback improved earlier fastener designs, helping make the modern zipper practical. An interesting invention can look very small. Its usefulness comes from the way many parts meet, not from one giant hook.
Khóa kéo ghép hai hàng phần tử nhờ con trượt. Sundback cải tiến thiết kế trước đó để khóa kéo thực dụng hơn.

Think of a small black travel bag. A person can pack clothing inside: pants, a sock, a belt, a suit and a tie. A pocket may have its own zipper. Unlike a string, the fastener does not require the user to tie a knot each time. It offers a different way to join two edges.
Túi du lịch minh họa đồ đạc và cách khóa kéo nối mép mà không cần buộc nút mỗi lần.

Imagine two twin brothers packing for a trip. One twin has curly hair; the other is folding a towel. Their washing has just finished, and the bag will keep the clean items together after the wash. “The blue bag is mine, and the black one is yours,” one says. A friend's jacket is hers, while another traveller's uniform is his. This is a fictional example of everyday use, not the inventor's family history.
Hai anh em sinh đôi là nhân vật giả định để luyện từ và sở hữu, không phải gia đình nhà phát minh.

The brothers tidy the table until it looks tidy. A thin label distinguishes the bags. An adult coat and a teenage fashion item can both use the same basic fastening idea. Someone may buy a jacket for a celebration, plan to marry, or listen to a music single while dressing. The fastening does not depend on the occasion. Each single element must meet the next one properly. A user may be surprised by how much engineering sits in a familiar object. A smooth movement of the hand hides many small connections working together.
Một cơ chế có thể dùng trên nhiều kiểu quần áo. Chuyển động đơn giản của tay che nhiều kết nối nhỏ cần ăn khớp chính xác.

title: Bác sĩ chú ý đến đôi tay
englishTitle: The Doctor Who Looked at Hands
paragraphs: In 1847, Ignaz Semmelweis introduced a hand-cleaning procedure in a maternity clinic in Vienna. Deaths fell sharply after the change. The story became an important part of medical history. He compared what happened carefully. Observing patterns in a hospital could challenge accepted ideas about disease and the way doctors worked.
Năm 1847 tại Vienna, Semmelweis đưa quy trình làm sạch tay vào khoa sản; tử vong giảm mạnh. Ông so sánh kết quả để đặt câu hỏi về thực hành đang được chấp nhận.

A patient entered the clinic for care, yet contact during treatment could carry danger. Semmelweis linked the problem with material carried on doctors' hands. His explanation came before the modern understanding of germs was established. Doctors did not always know why a procedure helped. Their knowledge of medicine was still changing, and a useful observation did not mean they understood every cause.
Ông liên hệ vấn đề với chất mang trên tay bác sĩ, trước khi hiểu biết vi trùng hiện đại được thiết lập.

This history does not say that every illness has the same cause. Flu involves a virus, while a broken bone, a headache or a stomach problem may involve different issues. A dentist works on teeth; a heart specialist studies another part of the body. These comparisons help us avoid treating all health words as synonyms. A drug and a cleaning procedure are not identical kinds of intervention.
Các bệnh và vấn đề cơ thể không đồng nghĩa; thuốc khác quy trình làm sạch. Đây là so sánh từ vựng, không chẩn đoán.

People used to explain many hospital infections differently. A serious problem could leave a person ill and weak, and a change in their condition required attention. It was necessary to care about what happened before a new practice began and after it was introduced. Semmelweis's work reminds us that being careful includes examining results, not only looking tidy or removing visible blood. The major lesson is the value of evidence in efforts to prevent harm. Good intentions alone do not prove a method is all right. Doing good requires checking whether people's lives actually improve.
Bài học lịch sử là quan sát bằng chứng trước–sau thay đổi. Ý tốt hay vẻ sạch sẽ chưa đủ chứng minh hiệu quả chăm sóc.

title: Căn bệnh được thế giới chặn lại
englishTitle: A Disease the World Stopped
paragraphs: In 1980, the World Health Organization declared smallpox eradicated. This meant the disease no longer spread naturally among people. It was a historic achievement in medicine. A vaccination effort and careful searches for cases helped make it possible. Health workers worked together across many places. The result was larger than the work of one famous person.
Năm 1980, WHO tuyên bố thanh toán đậu mùa: bệnh không còn lây truyền tự nhiên giữa người. Tiêm chủng và tìm ca bệnh cùng hợp tác rộng lớn tạo nên thành quả.

Smallpox was a serious disease caused by a virus. A patient could become very ill, and the effects could be severe. The history of vaccination included Edward Jenner's work in 1796, but the later global campaign required much more. Workers repeatedly looked for cases. Finding an illness and responding mattered alongside the vaccine itself.
Đậu mùa là bệnh vi rút nghiêm trọng. Jenner là một phần lịch sử, không phải toàn bộ chiến dịch toàn cầu.

To understand the scale of the achievement, separate related words. A drug used for treatment is not automatically a vaccine. Flu is not smallpox. A dentist and a heart doctor have different roles, just as bone, blood and stomach name different things. A headache alone does not tell the whole story of a person's condition. These vocabulary comparisons are not a method for diagnosing disease.
Thuốc, vắc xin, cúm và tên các bộ phận cơ thể khác nhau. So sánh từ không phải phương pháp chẩn đoán.

Smallpox used to threaten communities around the world. International medical care and cooperation were necessary to prevent further spread. A system could not be weak at finding cases simply because other areas were doing well. People needed to care about distant communities as well as their own. They had to be careful before declaring the work finished. The major success did much good, but it did not make every health problem disappear. The world was not suddenly all right. The story shows what coordinated effort can achieve without pretending that one victory solves every challenge.
Cần giám sát và phối hợp trước khi tuyên bố hoàn tất. Chiến thắng đậu mùa không đồng nghĩa mọi bệnh khác biến mất.

title: Não không tắt khi bạn ngủ
englishTitle: Your Brain Does Not Switch Off at Night
paragraphs: When someone is asleep, the brain does not simply stop working. Sleep includes different stages, and brain activity changes through them. Sleep also supports memory and learning. A sleeping brain is more active than the idea of a switched-off machine suggests. This is why calling sleep “doing nothing” misses an important part of the story.
Não vẫn hoạt động trong các giai đoạn ngủ. Ngủ hỗ trợ trí nhớ và học tập, không phải “tắt máy”.

You may dream, although not every dream is remembered. A strange thought can seem normal until you wake up. The mind is still active, but it is not doing exactly the same work as daytime thinking. Scientists continue studying how sleep and memories connect. We should not turn that fact into a promise that sleep alone teaches words we have never studied.
Giấc mơ có thể bị quên. Khoa học về ngủ không hứa rằng chỉ ngủ sẽ học được từ chưa từng học.

Imagine a student preparing for a difficult test. The student feels nervous, becomes worried and begins to worry about every mistake. “Attention!” says a teacher in this imagined scene. “Do you mind stopping for a moment?” The teacher wants to stress the difference between useful study and endless stress. A short rest is not the same as a full night's sleep, but time to rest can change the study session.
Học sinh và giáo viên trong đoạn là tình huống tưởng tượng để phân biệt căng thẳng, nhấn mạnh và nghỉ ngơi.

Without enough sleep, learning and concentration can suffer. A task may go badly, and the next attempt may feel worse. Calling yourself the worst student does not explain the problem. An awful evening can make someone unhappy, but one evening is not a complete measure of ability. A classroom notice might remind learners to plan study time. Perhaps the right focus is the routine, not self-blame. It is likely that many factors matter. We should expect to practise and focus while awake; thinking little about study and hoping for a magical night is not the message.
Thiếu ngủ có thể ảnh hưởng tập trung, nhưng một buổi học tệ không xác định toàn bộ năng lực. Bài nhấn mạnh học và luyện lúc thức, không kỳ vọng phép màu.

title: Khoảng trống nhỏ bạn thường không thấy
englishTitle: The Small Gap You Usually Do Not See
paragraphs: Each eye has a small blind spot where the optic nerve leaves the retina. There are no light-detecting cells at that point. Yet everyday vision does not usually look like a picture with a dark hole. The brain uses surrounding information, and the other eye often supplies information too. Seeing is more complex than receiving a perfect photograph.
Mỗi mắt có điểm mù tại nơi dây thần kinh thị giác rời võng mạc. Não và thông tin từ mắt kia giúp trải nghiệm thường ngày không giống hình có lỗ đen.

In a simple demonstration, a mark can disappear when one eye is covered and the other looks at a fixed point from a suitable distance. It can then return when the distance changes. The most surprising part is the missing mark. This does not mean the paper changed. The demonstration shows something about the viewer's visual system.
Trong minh họa phù hợp, dấu trên giấy biến mất rồi trở lại khi đổi khoảng cách. Giấy không đổi; hệ nhìn tạo hiệu ứng.

Imagine a museum teacher saying, “Attention! Keep your focus on the fixed point. Do you mind trying again?” A notice explains the activity. Visitors may expect a trick, become nervous or feel worried that they did it badly. There is no need to describe one attempt as awful or call someone the worst observer. Moving the paper can make the result better or worse because position matters.
Giáo viên bảo tàng là tình huống giả định. Vị trí và điểm nhìn ảnh hưởng kết quả, không phải cuộc thi người quan sát giỏi nhất.

The teacher can stress that the mind interprets information rather than simply storing a camera image. This is not a memory test. A sudden thought or too much thinking about success can distract someone who is trying to focus. Perhaps an unhappy visitor wants a rest; they can rest and return. To worry adds stress, not evidence. The effect does not require sleep or being asleep, and you need not dream to see it. Looking more carefully is likely to teach us something, even when we initially think little about it. A missing dot can reveal a surprisingly active process behind ordinary sight.
Đây không phải bài kiểm tra trí nhớ hoặc giấc mơ. Dấu biến mất cho thấy nhìn là quá trình xử lý thông tin chủ động.

title: Người tìm hóa thạch bên bờ biển
englishTitle: The Fossil Hunter on the Shore
paragraphs: Mary Anning collected fossils near Lyme Regis on England's south coast. Her brother Joseph found an important skull, and Mary uncovered the rest of the skeleton. It belonged to an ichthyosaur, an ancient marine reptile. An animal in the sea was not necessarily a fish. Careful work could reveal a better explanation than a quick guess.
Mary Anning tìm hóa thạch ở Lyme Regis. Joseph tìm sọ, Mary khai quật phần còn lại của bộ xương bò sát biển ichthyosaur.

Anning's discoveries helped people understand prehistoric life. She worked herself, but her story also includes family, buyers and scientists. Her brother did not uncover the entire skeleton by himself. It is useful to support accurate history rather than turn one person into a hero who did everything alone. Evidence is as important as an exciting story.
Khám phá quan trọng nhưng không nên kể như một người làm tất cả. Bằng chứng quan trọng ngang sự hấp dẫn.

Her work also raises questions about opportunity. An independent collector did not have the same position as every established scientist. Being a female in a world where many recognized scientific positions belonged to a male affected access. Calling someone a clever lady or an unusual guy tells us less than describing the actual work. A national reputation or an award is not the only measure of what a person can achieve.
Cơ hội và vị trí của nữ người sưu tập độc lập khác các nhà khoa học được công nhận. Giải thưởng không phải thước đo duy nhất.

For a present-day learning exercise, imagine a museum planning an exhibition. The team must make a decision about whose work to include. One choice is a simple hero story; an alternative is to show the wider evidence. The second option may allow visitors to understand more. The team should accept well-supported claims and refuse invented details. Asking for permission to use a photograph is another task. “I can check this myself,” a learner might say, “but we should ask ourselves what we still do not know.” That gives future visitors a better chance to learn. We can succeed in telling an interesting story without pretending Anning could never fail or never needed support.
Nhóm bảo tàng hiện đại là ví dụ giả định: chọn trình bày bằng chứng, xin phép hình ảnh và thừa nhận điều chưa biết thay vì bịa chi tiết anh hùng.

title: Ngôi sao điện ảnh với ý tưởng vô tuyến
englishTitle: The Film Star with a Radio Idea
paragraphs: Hedy Lamarr was a film star, but acting was not her only interest. Working with composer George Antheil, she developed an idea for communication that changed radio frequencies in a coordinated pattern. Their work became a patent during the Second World War. The aim was to make a signal harder to interfere with.
Hedy Lamarr và George Antheil phát triển ý tưởng đổi tần số phối hợp, nhằm làm tín hiệu khó bị gây nhiễu; công trình được cấp bằng thời Thế chiến II.

This does not mean Lamarr built every modern wireless device herself. Antheil did not do all the work by himself either. Their invention was an important part of a wider history. A better account explains the partnership. We can support recognition without making a false claim that one hero invented the whole internet.
Điều đó không có nghĩa Lamarr tự tạo mọi thiết bị không dây hoặc cả internet. Cần nói đúng quan hệ hợp tác.

A person's public image is not as complete as their full life. Calling someone a glamorous lady or a musical guy may hide other skills. A female and a male could contribute different knowledge to the same problem. Independent future inventors can learn from that choice to work together. To achieve something new may require an opportunity, a chance to test ideas and practical support, not only talent.
Hình ảnh công chúng không phản ánh toàn bộ kỹ năng. Cơ hội, thử nghiệm và hỗ trợ cũng quan trọng.

Imagine students preparing a short presentation about the patent. They have a decision to make: accept an exciting but exaggerated headline, or refuse it and check the evidence. An alternative explanation can still be interesting. One option is to compare a changing signal with people following the same changing schedule. This is an analogy, not the complete engineering. “I cannot explain every detail myself,” a student might say, “but we can ask ourselves which claims are supported.” They need permission for some images and should allow time to check them. A national honour or an award can recognize work, but it does not prove every popular story. We succeed more honestly when we admit where a simple explanation may fail.
Nhóm học sinh là giả định: kiểm tra tiêu đề, phân biệt ví von với giải thích kỹ thuật đầy đủ, thừa nhận giới hạn thay vì phóng đại.

title: Ý tưởng sau một trận chiến
englishTitle: An Idea After a Battlefield
paragraphs: In 1859, Henry Dunant saw the suffering left by the Battle of Solferino. Many wounded people needed help. He later wrote about the experience and called for better care. His ideas helped lead to the committee founded in 1863 that became the International Committee of the Red Cross. A personal experience became a wider project.
Dunant chứng kiến hậu quả Solferino năm 1859, viết về trải nghiệm và kêu gọi chăm sóc tốt hơn. Ý tưởng góp phần hình thành ủy ban năm 1863.

During war, an army may see another soldier as an enemy. A wounded person still needs care, whether that person is an officer or an ordinary member of the force. Helping is not the same as celebrating a victory. It was such a serious problem that a wider response was needed. Wanting peace did not remove the immediate need to help people who were already hurt.
Người bị thương vẫn cần giúp đỡ dù thuộc bên nào. Muốn hòa bình không xóa nhu cầu cứu trợ trước mắt.

Think about how a community learns from this history. A school might invite a guest to explain the role of humanitarian work in society. A local charity could organize an informal discussion about social responsibility. These are possible modern activities, not events recorded at Solferino. Being polite is helpful, but politeness alone is not enough. Practical organization matters too.
Buổi thảo luận cộng đồng là khả năng hiện đại, không sự kiện tại Solferino. Lịch sự cần đi với tổ chức thực tế.

Imagine receiving an invitation to attend that discussion. A helpful host can greet visitors in a friendly manner and offer a warm welcome. A learner might say, “Sir, may I ask a question?” Another might react, “Oh dear, that was terrible,” before asking how help was organized after. “All right, let's examine the evidence,” could be the reply. None of this dialogue is a historical quotation. The aim is not to celebrate suffering or be rude about victims. It is to understand the possibility of turning concern into organized help, even when the people who need it belong to opposing sides.
Lời thoại minh họa không phải trích dẫn lịch sử. Mục tiêu là hiểu cách biến quan tâm thành giúp đỡ có tổ chức, không tôn vinh đau khổ.

title: Buddy và con phố đông
englishTitle: Buddy and a Busy Street
paragraphs: In 1928, Morris Frank returned to the United States with Buddy, a dog trained to guide him. He had learned to work with her in Switzerland. In New York, they crossed a busy street in front of reporters. The demonstration showed a practical partnership. The street was too busy for a careless crossing.
Năm 1928, Morris Frank về Mỹ cùng chó dẫn đường Buddy sau huấn luyện tại Thụy Sĩ. Họ qua phố đông trước phóng viên ở New York.

Frank later helped establish The Seeing Eye with Dorothy Harrison Eustis. The organization began in 1929. Training was important: a guide dog was not simply a pet wearing a special label. It was such a useful partnership that the demonstration attracted attention. The dog's role involved learning, and the person also learned to work with the dog.
Frank và Eustis sau đó đồng sáng lập The Seeing Eye, bắt đầu năm 1929. Cả người lẫn chó đều cần học phối hợp.

This history opens a wider question about society and independence. A community can offer a welcome while still creating barriers. A building may invite a guest but fail to consider access. A charity can be helpful through training and education, while social attitudes affect everyday life. An army officer or a soldier may receive guide-dog support in one context; a civilian may need it in another. The need is not limited to war or peace.
Sự chào đón bằng lời chưa chắc đã tạo khả năng tiếp cận. Đào tạo và thái độ xã hội ảnh hưởng tính độc lập.

Imagine an informal school event to celebrate this history. Students receive an invitation to attend, then greet the speaker in a polite manner. “Sir, may I ask about the training?” is a possible question. “Oh dear, I thought the dog did everything alone,” is another invented reaction. “All right, let's learn how both partners work,” could follow. These are learning examples, not Frank's recorded words. Being rude or distracting a working dog would miss the point. People can discuss the possibility of greater independence and reflect on the event after. The real story is about a trained team, not a magical animal that needs no human partnership.
Sự kiện trường học và lời thoại là ví dụ tưởng tượng. Trọng tâm là đội phối hợp được huấn luyện, không phải con vật thần kỳ làm mọi việc một mình.

title: Một tòa tháp, nhiều vai trò
englishTitle: One Tower, Many Jobs
paragraphs: The Tower of London is more than one tall building. It is a complex that has served as a fortress, a royal palace and a prison. Building work began under William the Conqueror in the eleventh century. The White Tower stands inside the wider fortress. Different parts belong to different moments in a long history.
Tháp London là quần thể từng làm pháo đài, cung điện và nhà tù. Các phần thuộc nhiều thời kỳ; việc xây dựng bắt đầu dưới William thời thế kỷ XI.

A castle can protect a ruler and display power to the population. A king or queen may live behind strong walls, but walls also send a message to people outside. A government can use buildings to show the strength of the state. That is different from saying every ruler was a president, or that every country had the same system of law.
Lâu đài vừa bảo vệ vừa thể hiện quyền lực. Không nên áp cùng mô hình chính trị cho mọi quốc gia, thời kỳ.

The Tower's history includes people held prisoner and people put to death. An attack, a fight, an order to attack or to fight can have serious human consequences. A gun is only one possible weapon; the ability to kill did not begin with guns. The long story should not be reduced to an exciting collection of weapons. Nor should every ancient or old building be treated as if its people shared one united opinion.
Lịch sử giam giữ và xử tử có hậu quả con người; không chỉ là bộ sưu tập vũ khí gây kích thích.

Today, public interest brings members of the public to learn about the site. A visitor may ask about a church, a ruler's belief in god, or the work of a lawyer defending someone. Such questions need evidence. Such is the challenge of history: buildings survive more easily than complete accounts of every life. A nearby pub and a modern street belong to another layer of the city, not necessarily the same period as the wall beside them. Keep those layers separate. Looking beyond the usual dramatic story reveals a place that changed its jobs over centuries.
Khách cần bằng chứng cho câu hỏi về tôn giáo và luật. Phố, quán hiện đại và tường cổ có thể thuộc các lớp thời gian khác nhau.

title: Bức tường không được xây trong một lần
englishTitle: The Wall That Was Not Built in One Go
paragraphs: The Great Wall of China is not one unchanged wall built at one moment. Earlier fortifications were joined under Qin Shi Huang around 220 BC, and construction continued through later periods. Work continued in the Ming period. The result includes walls, towers, passes and other defensive structures. Towers stand along different sections of the wall.
Vạn Lý Trường Thành gồm các công trình qua nhiều thời kỳ. Khoảng 220 TCN, các đoạn phòng thủ trước đó được nối; xây dựng tiếp tục tới các thời sau, gồm Minh.

The aim was to create a united defence system from places that had once been separate. An attack could threaten a border, and guards might have to fight. But a wall's story is not only a fight. Building, supplying and maintaining it required work from a large population. A government needed organization as well as the power to order people to act for the state.
Phòng thủ cần tổ chức xây, cung ứng và duy trì, không chỉ chiến đấu.

To read history carefully, distinguish institutions. A Chinese emperor was not simply a European king, a queen or a modern president with a different title. A palace, a castle, a prison, a church and a pub are not interchangeable buildings. Beliefs about a god, the work of a lawyer and the meaning of law also depend on time and place. These comparisons do not claim that every listed institution stood on the Great Wall.
Không đồng nhất chức danh, luật, niềm tin hay loại công trình giữa các nền văn hóa. Danh sách so sánh không khẳng định tất cả tồn tại trên tường thành.

Nor should a picture of a gun make us imagine the same weapon in every ancient period. To attack or kill is an action; explaining why it happened requires context. The public often sees one beautiful photograph and imagines a single continuous project. Public understanding improves when we ask which section, which period and which workers the picture represents. Such is the value of a careful question. The usual short description, “a very long wall,” is a beginning, but it leaves out centuries of changes and the lives behind the stones.
Một ảnh đẹp chưa đại diện mọi đoạn và thời kỳ. Hỏi ai xây, khi nào, ở đâu giúp vượt khỏi mô tả đơn giản “tường rất dài”.

title: Hồ sơ vân tay trước thời máy tính
englishTitle: A Fingerprint File Before Computers
paragraphs: In 1924, the US Bureau of Investigation brought fingerprint collections together in a national identification system. This was long before a quick computer search became familiar. Examiners compared records on cards. Information travelled from local offices to a central collection. A record could help connect information held in different places.
Năm 1924, cơ quan điều tra Mỹ tập hợp các bộ vân tay trong hệ nhận dạng quốc gia. Nhân viên so sánh thẻ giấy trước tìm kiếm máy tính.

A detective investigating a crime needs more than a strange story. A thief may steal an object, but deciding which person did it requires evidence. The fact that a print exists is not a complete account of when or why it was left. Fingerprints have been used for identification for many years. Identification and proving every part of a case are different tasks.
Nhận dạng không tự chứng minh toàn bộ vụ việc hoặc thời điểm dấu được để lại.

Imagine a classroom discussion about a fictional missing box. Students search for clues, question witnesses and report what they found. One argument concerns a print near the box. Another student may disagree and argue that the owner touched it yesterday. This invented example is not advice on investigating a real case. Its purpose is to separate observation from conclusion.
Chiếc hộp mất là tình huống lớp học hư cấu để phân biệt quan sát và kết luận, không hướng dẫn điều tra thật.

A reporter or journalist should not turn a comment into a certain answer merely because the media want an exciting headline. A secret meeting and a hidden secret belong to many stories, but they are not necessary for every explanation. Suppose someone says, “Sure, we can check, but that person looks guilty.” Appearance does not establish that they are a criminal. A careful review asks what actually supports the claim. To review the evidence and continue the discussion is better than saying “definitely” without enough information. The old cards show the value of organized records; they do not turn every mark into a complete story.
Ngoại hình, lời nhận xét hoặc tiêu đề hấp dẫn chưa đủ kết tội. Hồ sơ có giá trị nhưng mỗi dấu không kể trọn câu chuyện.

title: Hóa thạch hóa ra là giả
englishTitle: The Fossil That Was a Fake
paragraphs: In 1912, the Piltdown discovery was presented as an important clue to human origins. In 1953, it was exposed as a hoax. The material combined human skull pieces with an ape's jaw. Tests and close examination showed that the story did not fit the objects. The claim had attracted attention for decades.
Piltdown được công bố năm 1912 như dấu vết nguồn gốc người, rồi bị vạch là giả năm 1953. Mảnh sọ người được ghép với hàm vượn.

The teeth showed signs of alteration, and material had been made to look older. Evidence moved from the objects into a new explanation. A strange combination that once seemed exciting became a warning about accepting what people hope to find. The case was not solved by a dramatic detective running through a dark room. Careful scientific work changed the conclusion.
Kiểm tra răng và vật liệu làm cũ thay đổi kết luận. Đây là công việc khoa học cẩn thận, không cảnh thám tử kịch tính.

To understand the difference, compare it with an ordinary crime story. A thief might steal something, while a fraud changes what people believe about an object. The word criminal is not a substitute for proving a person's actions. A secret plan or a secret may interest a reporter, but a journalist still needs evidence. The media can report a claim without making it true.
Phân biệt trộm đồ và làm sai niềm tin về đồ vật. Truyền thông đăng khẳng định không tự biến nó thành thật.

Researchers had to question the old account, search for explanations and carry out a new review. A search for truth can involve people who disagree and argue, but an argument should be tested. In a classroom discussion, suppose a student says, “Sure, I can look again. It looks ancient.” Another can ask what actually establishes its age. That invented comment illustrates the problem; it is not a historical quote. To review an exciting idea is not to reject all discoveries. Saying something is definitely genuine requires more than its appearance. Piltdown remains memorable because testing eventually corrected a story that many people had accepted.
Lời thoại học sinh là minh họa. Kiểm tra lại không có nghĩa phủ nhận mọi phát hiện; Piltdown cho thấy bằng chứng có thể sửa câu chuyện từng được tin.

title: Một mét dài bao nhiêu?
englishTitle: How Long Is One Metre?
paragraphs: A metre seems ordinary until two people disagree about the length of their rulers. A shared unit helps them compare measurements. In the past, the international metre was represented by a carefully kept physical standard. In 1889, an international prototype was approved. Later definitions changed, and the modern metre is linked to the speed of light.
Mét cần định nghĩa chung. Chuẩn vật lý quốc tế được phê chuẩn năm 1889; định nghĩa về sau thay đổi và nay gắn tốc độ ánh sáng.

During a measurement, the unit matters. While one person measures, another can record the result. This is not just a problem for advanced mathematics. School maths uses shared meanings too. A square table and a circle on paper have different shapes, but both can be measured. A city square is a place, not automatically a perfect geometric shape.
Đơn vị quan trọng trong mọi phép đo. Hình vuông và quảng trường là hai nghĩa khác nhau của square.

Imagine a classroom survey of desk lengths. Students mark the starting position, then put a mark at the other end. They circle an unusual answer and check it again. The middle desk may stand in the middle of the room without having the average length. The mean is calculated from measurements, not from where furniture stands.
Khảo sát bàn là ví dụ lớp học: đánh dấu đầu đo, kiểm tra kết quả lạ. Bàn đứng giữa không tự có chiều dài trung bình.

To make progress, compare a specific result with the general pattern. A particular ruler may have a damaged edge. That is one factor that can create an apparent increase in length. Moving the starting point can increase an error; careful alignment can reduce it. Students should wait until everyone finishes before comparing totals. By the end, they may be certain which method they used. Of two badly placed rulers, neither gives a reliable result; with two suitable ones, either may work. If several disagree, check the method. The simple lesson behind the metre's history is powerful: a number needs a shared meaning before it can help people agree.
Thước và cách đặt ảnh hưởng sai số. Con số chỉ giúp so sánh khi người đo dùng ý nghĩa và phương pháp chung.

title: Gói kẹo cao su phát tiếng bíp
englishTitle: The Gum That Went Beep
paragraphs: On 26 June 1974, a pack of Wrigley's chewing gum was scanned at a supermarket checkout in Troy, Ohio. It became a famous first commercial UPC barcode scan. A small purchase marked a change in retail. The lines on the packet connected a product with information in a system, rather than being a decorative pattern.
Ngày 26/6/1974, gói kẹo Wrigley được quét UPC ở quầy siêu thị Troy, Ohio. Mã nối sản phẩm với dữ liệu, không chỉ trang trí.

During a sale, a scanner reads a code. While the customer waits, the system can look up information. The code needs a specific structure, not any random mark. A square modern code may look different from a traditional row of bars. A circle drawn around a product name is not automatically a barcode, and a town square has no role in reading it.
Máy đọc cấu trúc mã để tra thông tin; hình vẽ bất kỳ không tự thành mã vạch.

For a simple classroom exercise, label three objects with numbers. Mark each label clearly, then circle one item on a separate list. This teaches an idea behind identification, not the complete technology. In mathematics, or maths at school, a number may describe an amount. Here it identifies a particular item. A product unit and its identifying number are related but not identical concepts.
Đánh số đồ vật trong lớp chỉ minh họa nhận dạng, không mô tả đầy đủ công nghệ. Số định danh khác số lượng.

Imagine a survey of checkout times. The middle customer in a line is not necessarily the average customer by waiting time. The position in the middle tells us something different. Before claiming progress, examine a general pattern and be certain what was measured. One factor may increase speed while another causes an increase in delay. Better organization can reduce some delays. By the end of the exercise, the class has a table of results. If two labels are unreadable, neither helps; if both are valid, either may identify its item. If several are confused, fix the records. The first beep was memorable because the code belonged to a coordinated system.
Khảo sát thời gian chờ cần phân biệt vị trí giữa với giá trị trung bình, kiểm tra nhãn và dữ liệu. Tiếng bíp có ý nghĩa vì cả hệ thống phối hợp.

title: Lịch sử có trước công viên
englishTitle: A Park with a History Before the Park
paragraphs: Yellowstone became a national park in 1872. Its unusual natural features helped make it famous, but people had lived in and used the region for thousands of years before that date. Visitors can learn about more than scenery. The park's legal beginning was not the beginning of human history in the place.
Yellowstone thành công viên năm 1872, nhưng con người đã sống và sử dụng khu vực từ hàng nghìn năm trước. Mốc pháp lý không phải khởi đầu lịch sử con người.

A traveller arriving from abroad may see it first as a destination for tourism. A foreign visitor may book an airline ticket, arrange a stay and ask at a hotel reception about a tour. A guide can guide people through a story that includes landscapes and human lives. A long wait for a photograph should not become the only memory of the experience.
Khách có thể đặt chuyến đi và nhờ hướng dẫn tìm hiểu cảnh quan lẫn đời sống, thay vì chỉ chờ chụp ảnh.

Imagine a family planning an adventure. They pick a camp and ask where they can camp. Camping is a way to stay close to the landscape, but it does not mean a person may enter every area or sleep anywhere they like. “Is there anywhere suitable for our group?” is a better planning question. They might need to choose a different place. This is an example of planning, not current travel advice.
Gia đình cắm trại là ví dụ kế hoạch, không tư vấn du lịch hiện hành. Cắm trại không đồng nghĩa được vào mọi chỗ.

At a visitor centre, the family might look for a map somewhere near the desk. They want somewhere quiet to discuss it before moving forward. A back entrance and a path that goes past may look inviting, but appearance alone does not give permission to pass through. The family could learn the local history before setting out. The most interesting journey is not always the longest route. Recognizing that a celebrated park has a deeper human past makes the visit richer than a collection of beautiful views alone.
Tìm bản đồ và hiểu lịch sử trước khi đi giúp trải nghiệm sâu hơn. Cửa hay đường có vẻ mời gọi không tự cho quyền đi qua.

title: Khởi đầu chỉ mười hai dặm
englishTitle: The Twelve-Mile Beginning
paragraphs: In 1841, Thomas Cook organized a train excursion from Leicester to Loughborough. The journey was only about twelve miles. The passengers were travelling to a temperance meeting, connected with a movement against alcohol use. It was not a modern beach holiday. People could travel together through a planned arrangement.
Năm 1841, Cook tổ chức chuyến tàu khoảng 12 dặm Leicester–Loughborough để dự cuộc họp phong trào hạn chế rượu, không phải nghỉ biển hiện đại.

Cook's later business helped develop organized tourism, including journeys abroad. But the early experience began close to home. A traveller did not need a foreign destination to join that first trip. There was no modern airline involved. The adventure in this story was partly about organization: making it easier for a group to get from one place to another.
Doanh nghiệp về sau tổ chức du lịch xa hơn, nhưng khởi đầu gần nhà và dựa vào khả năng tổ chức nhóm.

Compare that with an imagined tour today. A customer may book a stay, meet a guide at reception and ask the guide to guide the group. After a wait, they enter a vehicle through a back door and move forward to their seats. A landscape goes past the windows as they pass through the countryside. These details illustrate present-day travel language; they are not a reconstruction of Cook's train.
Đoạn chuyến đi ngày nay là minh họa từ, không tái dựng toa tàu năm 1841.

An organized trip might reduce some planning work. It may still leave choices to make. Travellers can pick a hotel or a camp, choose to camp or decide that camping is not for them. They may want to go somewhere new and ask for somewhere suitable. “Can we stop anywhere?” is different from “Is anywhere available?” A plan answers questions about timing, places and shared responsibilities. The short 1841 excursion is memorable because a modest journey became part of a much larger travel story. Its importance does not depend on pretending it crossed the world in a single day.
Tour giảm một phần việc lên kế hoạch nhưng vẫn có lựa chọn. Chuyến ngắn đáng nhớ vì vai trò trong câu chuyện lớn hơn, không cần phóng đại quãng đường.

title: Phong bao mang nhiều hơn tiền
englishTitle: An Envelope Bigger Than Its Contents
paragraphs: Red envelopes are associated with Lunar New Year in many communities. In Chinese traditions, they can carry gifts of money and good wishes. Similar customs appear in other cultures, with local differences. A tradition can connect people without looking exactly the same in every family. We must distinguish a common custom from a universal rule.
Phong bao đỏ gắn Tết ở nhiều cộng đồng, mang tiền và lời chúc. Phong tục khác nhau theo nơi và gia đình; phổ biến không có nghĩa bắt buộc với tất cả.

A gift may strengthen a relationship, and the wish matters alongside the contents. People wish one another a good year. A lovely envelope may please the receiver, who feels pleased and thanks the giver happily. The envelope can also appear at occasions such as a wedding. It is not a ring, but both objects can carry meaning beyond their material value.
Quà giúp thể hiện quan hệ; ý nghĩa vượt vật chất, giống một số đồ dùng trong đám cưới.

Imagine a family preparing gifts. “Whose envelope is this?” asks one person. “And whose is the one beside it?” Another says, “Ah, this one is for our cousin.” A child replies, “Wow, the design is beautiful!” A surprise inside might surprise the receiver, but the amount should not become the whole story. A person can be surprised by a small thoughtful gift; expensive gifts are not the only surprising ones.
Lời thoại gia đình là minh họa, không đại diện mọi nhà. Quà nhỏ chu đáo vẫn gây vui và bất ngờ.

These invented speakers do not represent every family. Someone may be married, single or divorced, and customs about giving can differ. A typical practice in one place may be unusual elsewhere. You don't have to assume that one household speaks for everyone. A phone may ring as relatives exchange greetings, and a diary may record the visit. title: Tình bạn nở hoa
englishTitle: A Friendship That Blooms
paragraphs: In 1912, cherry trees from Japan were planted in Washington, DC, as a gift of friendship. Their flowers became a familiar part of the city's spring landscape. The gift connected a place with a relationship between people in two countries. A living gift changes with the seasons. It does not stay like a picture in a frame.
Năm 1912, cây anh đào từ Nhật được trồng tại Washington như quà hữu nghị. Quà sống thay đổi theo mùa, khác ảnh cố định.

The blossoms can create a lovely scene. Visitors may be surprised and pleased and take photographs happily. A typical spring visit is linked with the tradition of enjoying the flowers, but the exact timing depends on nature. It may surprise someone who expects a fixed date. A late or early bloom can be a surprise, and the changing timing is surprising only if we imagine trees follow our calendars.
Hoa tạo cảnh đẹp nhưng lịch nở phụ thuộc tự nhiên, không ngày cố định trên lịch khách.

Imagine friends planning a visit. “Whose camera shall we bring? Whose is this bag?” one asks. “Ah, it's mine,” another answers. “Wow, I hope we see the flowers!” They wish for good weather, but a wish is not a forecast. We have to distinguish a hope from a prediction. A promise about perfect weather would be unreliable, so they do not promise it.
Bạn bè lên kế hoạch là giả định. Mong trời đẹp khác dự báo hoặc lời hứa thời tiết.

One friend may write in a diary, while a phone begins to ring as the group leaves. A couple might choose the view for a wedding photograph and show a ring; another visitor may be single or divorced. These imagined visitors do not all share one life story. The flowers can please different people for different reasons. We mustn't treat every visitor as identical. An unusual personal memory may matter more than a famous photograph. Sadly, blossoms do not last forever. Yet their short season can help people notice the present and remember the history of a gift that still shapes a public landscape.
Khách có đời sống và ký ức khác nhau. Hoa ngắn ngày khuyến khích chú ý hiện tại và nhớ lịch sử món quà tạo nên cảnh quan công cộng.

title: Đời thứ hai của chiếc lon
englishTitle: A Can’s Second Life
paragraphs: An aluminium drink can does not have to end its story after one drink. The metal can be collected, processed and made into new products. Recycling aluminium generally needs much less energy than producing new metal from ore. We should distinguish that possibility from what happens to every individual can. A recyclable material still needs a working collection system.
Nhôm có thể được thu gom và tái chế, thường dùng ít năng lượng hơn làm từ quặng. Khả năng tái chế không đảm bảo từng lon thật sự được xử lý.

Imagine a community sorting day. A volunteer would like to explain the route from used can to new material. A plastic bag may contain rubbish, but not everything inside belongs in the same bin. Plastic and aluminium are different materials. To recycle them may involve different processes. The right route can depend on the local collection system, so this story does not give one universal sorting rule.
Ngày phân loại cộng đồng là ví dụ. Nhựa và nhôm cần quy trình khác; hướng dẫn tùy hệ thu gom địa phương.

The volunteers suggest checking the actual instructions. One suggestion is to provide clear labels and replace damaged signs. They consider a request for information about the next stage. It is rather easy to see the collection point and forget what happens after it. But a solution must deal with transport and processing too. A full bag beside a sign does not prove that recycling has happened.
Nhãn rõ và thông tin về công đoạn sau giúp ích. Bỏ vào thùng chưa chứng minh đã tái chế.

Environmental problems also have different sources. Smoke in the air is not the same as a can on the ground. A person who chooses to smoke may leave a cigarette end; smoking and litter involve more than one kind of impact. These examples show why one activity cannot solve every form of pollution. Communities can try to avoid unnecessary waste and control what happens to collected material. A second use for metal is valuable, but it does not make unlimited consumption harmless. Anyway, the can's next chapter is not automatic. People must continue the process beyond the moment when it disappears into a container.
Khói, đầu thuốc và lon bỏ đi là những vấn đề khác nhau. Tái sử dụng vật liệu có giá trị nhưng không khiến tiêu thụ vô hạn vô hại; quy trình phải tiếp tục sau thu gom.

title: Nhựa nhỏ đi nhưng chưa biến mất
englishTitle: The Plastic That Became Too Small to See
paragraphs: A plastic object in the sea may break into smaller and smaller pieces. That does not mean the material has completely disappeared. Many commonly used plastics remain as small fragments. Pieces under five millimetres are called microplastics. A large object can become harder to see while still being present in the environment.
Nhựa ngoài biển có thể vỡ nhỏ mà không biến mất hoàn toàn. Mảnh dưới 5 mm gọi là vi nhựa.

This is why a plastic bottle and tiny pieces of plastic belong to the same wider story. Visible rubbish is only part of pollution. A beach visitor may put a bottle in a bin, but pieces already in the water are harder to collect. We should not confuse “out of sight” with “gone”. A visitor might say, “I would like to understand where the pieces go.”
Rác nhìn thấy chỉ là phần của ô nhiễm; không thấy không đồng nghĩa không còn.

Imagine a group discussing a local cleanup. They suggest starting with waste they can safely collect. One suggestion is to provide better information, and another is to replace an unnecessary disposable object. They consider a request for more research. The next step will depend on the place and may involve several organizations. This is a planning example, not a claim that one cleanup can remove every tiny fragment from the sea.
Nhóm dọn rác là ví dụ kế hoạch, không tuyên bố một lần dọn sẽ lấy hết vi nhựa. Cách xử lý tùy địa điểm và nhiều bên.

The group must deal with different materials and sources. Smoke from burning waste does not prove the problem is solved. A cigarette end left by someone who chooses to smoke is another kind of litter; smoking also produces air pollution. The same simple solution cannot solve all these problems. It is rather tempting to choose one easy answer anyway, but evidence should guide the plan. People can try to avoid unnecessary waste, control losses and recycle suitable materials. A useful use today can still create waste tomorrow. The story of a fragment can continue long after the original object is no longer recognizable.
Đốt rác, khói và đầu thuốc không có một lời giải chung đơn giản. Cần bằng chứng, giảm thất thoát và xử lý phù hợp; vật liệu có thể tồn tại sau khi đồ vật không còn nhận ra.

title: Vì sao bong bóng tròn?
englishTitle: Why a Bubble Chooses a Round Shape
paragraphs: A soap bubble floating freely in still air tends to form a sphere. For a given amount of enclosed air, that shape has the smallest surface area. The thin film pulls inward. Soap changes the properties of water and helps the film last. It lowers surface tension rather than increasing it, a detail that surprises many people.
Bong bóng tự do trong không khí yên thường thành cầu, diện tích bề mặt nhỏ nhất cho thể tích khí đó. Xà phòng giảm sức căng bề mặt và giúp màng tồn tại.

This small object connects chemistry with forces and shapes. A toy bubble set can introduce a real question, not merely provide a toy to chase. We have seen bubbles in ordinary life, but familiarity is not an explanation. A learner may say, “I used to think soap made the pull stronger.” Learning can begin when that earlier idea changes.
Đồ chơi có thể gợi câu hỏi khoa học thật. Quen nhìn chưa có nghĩa đã hiểu cơ chế.

Imagine a supervised museum activity. “Shall we look before we touch?” asks a teacher. “Keep your finger away from your eyes and hold the frame steadily.” Visitors are used to seeing round bubbles. A quick movement can disturb the film. If people push, pull, shake or knock the frame, the result may change. They do not need to throw or drop it to make a useful observation.
Hoạt động bảo tàng là giả định có giám sát. Chuyển động khung làm thay kết quả; quan sát không cần ném hay làm rơi.

A child may jump with excitement, but a sudden jump beside the table could cause trouble. One useful tip is to compare only one change at a time. If a bubble breaks easily, the observer can react by asking why, rather than calling the activity stupid or the learner lazy. Someone may realize that a simple appearance hides several interacting factors. Looking closely can be done free of charge in many everyday situations, although not every museum activity is free. A tiny bubble offers a large lesson: first describe what happens, then test the reason you propose.
So sánh một thay đổi mỗi lần có ích hơn tự chê khi màng vỡ. Bài học là mô tả hiện tượng rồi kiểm tra lời giải thích.

title: Con cừu bay trước hành khách người
englishTitle: The Sheep That Flew Before People
paragraphs: In September 1783, a Montgolfier balloon carried a sheep, a duck and a rooster above Versailles. These animals were passengers in an early hot-air flight. Later that year, people made a free flight in a Montgolfier balloon. The animal flight belonged to a sequence of tests, not a modern airline service.
Tháng 9/1783, khí cầu Montgolfier chở cừu, vịt và gà trống ở Versailles. Cùng năm sau đó có chuyến bay tự do chở người. Đây là chuỗi thử nghiệm, không dịch vụ hàng không.

Hot air is less dense than the cooler air around it, which helps explain the lift. The balloon was not pulled upward by invisible wings. People used to explain unfamiliar flight through guesses. A correct explanation needs evidence about air and forces, not only a dramatic drawing. The movement could make observers react with surprise and realize that flight was becoming possible in a new way.
Không khí nóng có mật độ thấp hơn không khí lạnh xung quanh, góp phần tạo lực nâng. Hình vẽ kịch tính không thay lời giải thích có bằng chứng.

Compare a toy balloon model with the real vehicle. The model is a toy, not a safe passenger craft. You may hold its string with a finger, pull or push it, and touch its surface. If you shake it, knock it against a wall, throw it or drop it, you are studying a different situation. A model does not reproduce every force or risk of the original flight.
Mô hình đồ chơi không tái tạo mọi lực hoặc độ an toàn của khí cầu thật.

In an imagined class, someone asks, “Shall we compare a balloon with a bubble?” A soap film involves chemistry and surface tension, whereas hot-air lift involves differences in density. Learners have observed both, but the mechanisms differ. Students are used to comparing models with real objects. One child may jump in excitement; that jump is not the same as sustained flight. A useful tip is to ask what the model leaves out. Calling a failed idea stupid or a quiet learner lazy creates trouble, not understanding. Pictures may be viewed free online, but access alone does not explain them easily. The remarkable passengers are memorable; the patient testing behind their journey matters too.
Lớp học so sánh bong bóng và khí cầu là giả định. Cơ chế khác nhau; hiểu mô hình phải hỏi điều nó bỏ qua. Hành khách lạ đáng nhớ nhưng quá trình thử nghiệm cũng quan trọng.

title: Vở kịch radio nghe như bản tin
englishTitle: The Radio Play That Sounded Like News
paragraphs: On 30 October 1938, Orson Welles and his radio company broadcast an adaptation of The War of the Worlds. Parts sounded like news bulletins about an invasion from Mars. It was a drama, not a real invasion. Some listeners were frightened, but later stories of a whole nation in panic exaggerated the evidence.
Ngày 30/10/1938, Welles phát vở kịch War of the Worlds có phần giống bản tin. Một số người sợ, nhưng câu chuyện cả nước hoảng loạn về sau đã phóng đại bằng chứng.

The format drew attention because a speaker could present an imaginary event in the style of a serious announcement. Listeners might notice the urgent voice before checking the context. The background mattered: the programme was a performance. A look at its schedule or a check of other information could change the sense of what was heard. A confident personality or dramatic speech does not make every statement true.
Giọng khẩn cấp và phong cách thông báo dễ thu hút; cần biết bối cảnh đây là biểu diễn. Tự tin không bảo đảm thật.

Imagine a modern classroom talk or a small conference about the broadcast. A poster might show a frightened crowd, but the teacher should mention that one image cannot measure a country's reaction. When students refer to the event, they need to distinguish the play from the stories told about it. Evidence matters more than a memorable headline. Learners can get used to checking the source before repeating a claim.
Lớp học là giả định. Một ảnh đám đông không đo được phản ứng cả quốc gia; phải phân biệt vở kịch và huyền thoại về nó.

A kid may ask why something unreal can seem believable. Sounds can make an imagined scene appear vivid, and uncertainty does not disappear just because a voice sounds official. People may act on what they hear, complain about a programme or discuss it later. That is a matter worth understanding, but it does not prove everyone reacted alike either. I recommend comparing several sources, including accounts that question the popular legend. Details matter. The most useful lesson is not that all audiences are foolish. It is that an exciting story about a story also needs checking.
Phản ứng cá nhân không chứng minh tất cả giống nhau. Bài học là kiểm tra cả câu chuyện hấp dẫn được kể về một câu chuyện.

title: Khi trở về trở thành nhiệm vụ
englishTitle: When Coming Home Became the Mission
paragraphs: Apollo 13 left Earth in April 1970 with a plan to land on the Moon. An oxygen tank explosion changed the mission. The crew used the lunar module as a lifeboat while teams worked on bringing them home. All three astronauts returned safely on 17 April. The planned landing did not happen, but the return was a major achievement.
Apollo 13 rời Trái Đất tháng 4/1970 để đáp Mặt Trăng. Nổ bình ôxy khiến nhiệm vụ đổi; mô-đun Mặt Trăng làm nơi cứu sinh. Ba phi hành gia về an toàn ngày 17/4.

Clear communication became essential. A speaker had to present a problem accurately, and listeners had to notice important details. A dramatic speech alone could not repair the spacecraft. Engineers needed the background and context of each report. A quick look at one reading was not always enough; another check could help make sense of it. The crew had to get used to working in an unexpected living space.
Trao đổi chính xác, hiểu bối cảnh và kiểm tra số liệu quan trọng hơn bài nói kịch tính. Phi hành đoàn phải thích nghi không gian sống bất ngờ.

The response involved many people, including teams on the ground. One person's personality was not a complete explanation for the result. People had to act, share information and keep their attention on the changing situation. A problem might appear small at first or seem difficult to explain. It would not disappear because someone refused to mention it or chose only to complain. In an emergency, details matter.
Nhiều đội phối hợp, không chỉ một cá tính anh hùng. Bỏ qua hoặc không nói vấn đề không khiến nó biến mất.

Imagine a later classroom talk, rather than an actual mission conference. A kid points to a poster and asks whether the mission failed. The teacher can refer to two different goals: landing on the Moon and returning the crew. I recommend separating those goals before answering. The landing did not succeed, but saying nothing succeeded is not accurate either. That is a matter of defining the question carefully. The reasons for success matter too: teamwork, planning and tested solutions deserve attention alongside the danger. A mission can change its purpose without making the effort meaningless.
Lớp học giả định phân biệt hai mục tiêu: đáp Mặt Trăng và đưa người về. Mục tiêu đầu thất bại không có nghĩa không thành công điều gì; hợp tác và giải pháp có giá trị.

questions.q: In “People had to act, share information and keep their attention on the changing situation.”, what does “act” mean?
explanations: act ở đây là “hành động, diễn”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: to do something for a particular purpose or in order to deal with a situation
“sự chú ý” là nghĩa của attention; act ở đây nghĩa là “hành động, diễn”.
“đề xuất” là nghĩa của recommend; act ở đây nghĩa là “hành động, diễn”.

questions.q: In “People had to act, share information and keep their attention on the changing situation.”, what does “attention” mean?
explanations: “sự kiểm tra” là nghĩa của check; attention ở đây nghĩa là “sự chú ý”.
“có vẻ” là nghĩa của seem; attention ở đây nghĩa là “sự chú ý”.
attention ở đây là “sự chú ý”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: the act of listening to, looking at or thinking about something/somebody carefully; interest that people show in somebody/something

questions.q: In “A quick look at one reading was not always enough; another check could help make sense of it.”, what does “check” mean?
explanations: “xuất hiện” là nghĩa của appear; check ở đây nghĩa là “sự kiểm tra”.
check ở đây là “sự kiểm tra”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: an act of making sure that something is safe, correct or in good condition by examining it
“cái nhìn” là nghĩa của look; check ở đây nghĩa là “sự kiểm tra”.

questions.q: In “A quick look at one reading was not always enough; another check could help make sense of it.”, what does “look” mean?
explanations: look ở đây là “cái nhìn”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: an act of looking at somebody/something
“ý nghĩa, sự hợp lý” là nghĩa của sense; look ở đây nghĩa là “cái nhìn”.
“biến mất” là nghĩa của disappear; look ở đây nghĩa là “cái nhìn”.

questions.q: In “A quick look at one reading was not always enough; another check could help make sense of it.”, what does “sense” mean?
explanations: “vấn đề” là nghĩa của matter; sense ở đây nghĩa là “ý nghĩa, sự hợp lý”.
“phàn nàn” là nghĩa của complain; sense ở đây nghĩa là “ý nghĩa, sự hợp lý”.
sense ở đây là “ý nghĩa, sự hợp lý”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: an understanding about something; an ability to judge something

questions.q: In “That is a matter of defining the question carefully.”, what does “matter” mean?
explanations: “bao gồm” là nghĩa của including; matter ở đây nghĩa là “vấn đề”.
matter ở đây là “vấn đề”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: used (to ask) if somebody is upset, unhappy, etc. or if there is a problem
“đề cập” là nghĩa của mention; matter ở đây nghĩa là “vấn đề”.

questions.q: In “The reasons for success matter too: teamwork, planning and tested solutions deserve attention alongside the danger.”, what does “matter” mean?
explanations: matter ở đây là “quan trọng”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: to be important or have an important effect on somebody/something
“nói đến, tham chiếu” là nghĩa của refer; matter ở đây nghĩa là “quan trọng”.
“đứa trẻ” là nghĩa của kid; matter ở đây nghĩa là “quan trọng”.

questions.q: In “It would not disappear because someone refused to mention it or chose only to complain.”, what does “mention” mean?
explanations: “nói đến, tham chiếu” là nghĩa của refer; mention ở đây nghĩa là “đề cập”.
“đứa trẻ” là nghĩa của kid; mention ở đây nghĩa là “đề cập”.
mention ở đây là “đề cập”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: to write or speak about something/somebody, especially without giving much information

questions.q: In “The teacher can refer to two different goals: landing on the Moon and returning the crew.”, what does “refer” mean?
explanations: “người nói” là nghĩa của speaker; refer ở đây nghĩa là “nói đến, tham chiếu”.
refer ở đây là “nói đến, tham chiếu”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: to send somebody/something to somebody/something for help, advice or a decision
“đề xuất” là nghĩa của recommend; refer ở đây nghĩa là “nói đến, tham chiếu”.

questions.q: In “I recommend separating those goals before answering.”, what does “recommend” mean?
explanations: recommend ở đây là “đề xuất”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: to tell somebody that something is good or useful, or that somebody would be suitable for a particular job, etc.
“có vẻ” là nghĩa của seem; recommend ở đây nghĩa là “đề xuất”.
“bài phát biểu” là nghĩa của speech; recommend ở đây nghĩa là “đề xuất”.

questions.q: In “A problem might appear small at first or seem difficult to explain.”, what does “seem” mean?
explanations: “xuất hiện” là nghĩa của appear; seem ở đây nghĩa là “có vẻ”.
“buổi nói chuyện” là nghĩa của talk; seem ở đây nghĩa là “có vẻ”.
seem ở đây là “có vẻ”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: to give the impression of being or doing something

questions.q: In “A problem might appear small at first or seem difficult to explain.”, what does “appear” mean?
explanations: “hội nghị” là nghĩa của conference; appear ở đây nghĩa là “xuất hiện”.
appear ở đây là “xuất hiện”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: to start to be seen
“biến mất” là nghĩa của disappear; appear ở đây nghĩa là “xuất hiện”.

questions.q: In “It would not disappear because someone refused to mention it or chose only to complain.”, what does “disappear” mean?
explanations: disappear ở đây là “biến mất”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: to become impossible to see
“phàn nàn” là nghĩa của complain; disappear ở đây nghĩa là “biến mất”.
“trình bày” là nghĩa của present; disappear ở đây nghĩa là “biến mất”.

questions.q: In “It would not disappear because someone refused to mention it or chose only to complain.”, what does “complain” mean?
explanations: “cũng không” là nghĩa của either; complain ở đây nghĩa là “phàn nàn”.
“chú ý, nhận thấy” là nghĩa của notice; complain ở đây nghĩa là “phàn nàn”.
complain ở đây là “phàn nàn”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: to say that you are annoyed, unhappy or not satisfied about somebody/something

questions.q: In “The landing did not succeed, but saying nothing succeeded is not accurate either.”, what does “either” mean?
explanations: “áp phích” là nghĩa của poster; either ở đây nghĩa là “cũng không”.
either ở đây là “cũng không”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: used after negative phrases to state that a feeling or situation is similar to one already mentioned
“bao gồm” là nghĩa của including; either ở đây nghĩa là “cũng không”.

questions.q: In “The response involved many people, including teams on the ground.”, what does “including” mean?
explanations: including ở đây là “bao gồm”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: having something as part of a group or set
“đứa trẻ” là nghĩa của kid; including ở đây nghĩa là “bao gồm”.
“bối cảnh nền” là nghĩa của background; including ở đây nghĩa là “bao gồm”.

questions.q: In “A kid points to a poster and asks whether the mission failed.”, what does “kid” mean?
explanations: “người nói” là nghĩa của speaker; kid ở đây nghĩa là “đứa trẻ”.
“tính cách” là nghĩa của personality; kid ở đây nghĩa là “đứa trẻ”.
kid ở đây là “đứa trẻ”. Định nghĩa trong nguồn từ vựng: a child or young person

questions.q: She is gradually ___ living alone.
explanations: Be used to chỉ trạng thái đã quen, không nhấn quá trình dần quen như đề.
Mẫu cố định dùng used, không phải use.
Get used to nói quá trình dần thích nghi.

questions.q: She is getting used to ___ from home.
explanations: Get used to + V-ing; to là giới từ.
Không dùng nguyên mẫu sau giới từ to trong mẫu này.
V2/V3 không dùng thay V-ing ở đây.

questions.q: ___ he your teacher?
explanations: Does chỉ hỗ trợ động từ thường, không thay be trước teacher.
Do không thay be và không hòa hợp với he.
Teacher là danh từ; be tự đảo để hỏi, he dùng is.

questions.q: Nam usually ___ from home on Fridays.
explanations: Thiếu s với chủ ngữ số ít trong câu khẳng định.
V-ing không tự làm vị ngữ; cần be và ngữ cảnh tiếp diễn.
Chủ ngữ ngôi ba số ít: hiện tại đơn thêm s.

note: Bài học được biên soạn từ các nguồn được dẫn, có câu hỏi và ví dụ giả định để luyện tiếng Anh. Ví dụ giả định không phải lời nói hay sự kiện lịch sử được ghi chép. Định nghĩa từ lấy từ bộ dữ liệu từ vựng đang học; nghĩa Việt theo ngữ cảnh do ứng dụng biên soạn.
